stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber: wrote working Linux exploits for 948 flaws, found 81 new Firefox bugs, access limited to vetted defenders

articles.title: 오픈AI, 'GPT-6 사이버' 출시…취약점 공격 성공률 51% 향상
OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?

facts.fact: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Cyber on Nov 5 (US time); it is built on GPT-6 Astra (September) and specialised in finding vulnerabilities, writing exploit code and penetration testing.
Researchers reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and wrote working privilege-escalation exploits for 948; GPT-5.6 Sol succeeded on 166 in the same setup (over 5x fewer).
According to Reuters (as cited by AI타임스), 588 of the 948 were previously unknown flaws; OpenAI passed 304 serious issues with fixes to Linux developers.
It found 81 new high-severity vulnerabilities in Mozilla's Firefox and found 30 known ones were more severe than rated; Mozilla fixed many.
On ExploitGym it scored 48.5% vs 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber (a 51% relative gain); it did worse than GPT-6 Astra on FrontierCyber (90 of 288 tasks vs 96).
OpenAI rates its cyber capability 'Critical', the top tier of its safety framework, up from 'High' for GPT-5.6 Cyber.

Access is limited to approved customers of Daybreak Red, with identity and permission checks; OpenAI plans to widen it over the coming weeks and add a group for critical infrastructure (power plants, water treatment) defenders.
API price is $20 per million input tokens and $100 per million output tokens; context window about 1.05 million tokens.
Max Justicz, CTO of Charge Robotics, used GPT 5.6 Sol via OpenAI's Daybreak Blue program to find a severe Ubuntu/Debian flaw in two hours; Debian patched it and there is no known exploitation.
OpenAI says it wants to 'dramatically expand Daybreak' to organisations of every size, independent researchers and open-source maintainers.

stories.title: Anthropic gives Claude read-only access to your bank accounts with new Personal Finance beta

articles.title: Claude can now analyze your spending with its new Personal Finance tool
Anthropic lets Claude read your bank accounts, but not move money

facts.fact: Anthropic announced Personal Finance on Thursday; users connect bank and credit card accounts through Plaid and ask Claude about their money.
Access is read-only: Claude cannot move, manage or invest money.
Claude can add up monthly spending by category and flag duplicate charges, unexpected fees and steadily rising bills; it can explain terms like APR and calculate interest paid over the past year.
Claude sees each bank's name, account name and type, last four digits, balances, credit limits and up to two years of transactions.
Conversations in the Personal Finance hub are not used to train models; Anthropic says there are no ads or sponsored recommendations and it offers no cards, loans or savings accounts.
Beta rolls out this week to Pro, Max and Ultra plan users in the US.
OpenAI launched a similar ChatGPT feature in May, so TechCrunch says Claude is playing catch-up.
Users can link up to 16 US banks; for investment, loan and card accounts Claude reads only balances and credit limits.
Figures already shared stay in chats, artifacts and shared links until users delete them, even after a bank is unlinked; Anthropic warns Claude can make mistakes.
TNW notes that unlike Anthropic, OpenAI has started showing ads in ChatGPT.

카카오, '카나나' 불명예 철수…'카톡 올인' 반전 성공할까

facts.fact: Kakao unveiled 'Kanana Space', an AI assistant inside KakaoTalk; it will run a limited pilot for some users in December.
Users activate it by swiping two fingers down the phone screen; Kakao's mascot character Ryan appears mid-screen and answers by voice, with a text mode for public places.
Example given: asking it to summarise work-related KakaoTalk messages; it replies with what a project chat needs by 11 a.m.
Kakao is taking pre-registrations; a subset of applicants will join a closed beta test (CBT) at year-end.
Kakao shut down its standalone Kanana app and PC service on the 15th (Oct), 1 year 5 months after the beta began in May 2025.
Staff, infrastructure and marketing resources move to AI inside KakaoTalk, which has about 50 million users.
Plans include ordering, payments/transfers and bookings by voice command.

stories.title: Google makes Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video model generally available: 15-second clips, 30% cheaper

articles.title: Google's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash makes 15-second AI videos for less
Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips

facts.fact: Google made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available; clips are up to 15 seconds, up from 10.
Price is about $0.07 per second of 720p video via the Gemini API, down from $0.10 in June (30% cheaper).
Users can edit a clip over several chat turns (swap a product or background, change lighting) instead of regenerating.
In Google DeepMind's own comparisons, testers preferred 1.2 over 1.1 for visual consistency 62% of the time.
Rolling out in Flow, Google Vids, Google Ads and, for AI Ultra subscribers, the Gemini app; first time Omni is generally available on Google Cloud; every video carries an invisible SynthID watermark.
ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 (June) makes 30-second clips; Google is the only US company in the top 10 of one popular video ranking, where Chinese models hold the other nine spots.
Duration can be set in one-second steps from 3 to 15 seconds; drafts at 360p or 720p can be upscaled to 1080p or 4K.
Inputs can combine character, product or style images, motion clips up to three seconds and audio cues.

stories.title: Apple cuts employees' daily AI spending limits, Bloomberg reports; Tesla, Uber, Microsoft also tighten token budgets
stories.region: Europe angle (heise, Der Standard); source is Bloomberg via German outlets

articles.title: Apple kürzt interne KI-Budgets für Beschäftigte deutlich
Apple kürzt laut Medienbericht Budget für KI-Nutzung der Mitarbeiter

facts.fact: Per Bloomberg (citing insiders), Apple cut the daily AI spending limit for some engineers from $300 to $200 in October; further cuts to as low as $100 a day are planned for some engineering teams.
Non-engineering teams already capped at $100 a day may drop to $25; exceptions need senior-leader approval.
Employees can use Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini; some teams are told to move to cheaper or locally run models.
Apple declined to comment; new CEO John Ternus is reportedly pushing for a faster, leaner company with fewer management layers.

Tesla introduced a $200 weekly limit per employee; Uber capped single AI coding tools at $1,500 a month and used up its token budget in May; Microsoft tightened internal budgets; Meta set token budgets.
Der Standard (via Bloomberg): Apple cut the daily AI spend for some engineers from $300 to $200 last month, as part of broader cost cutting even though it wants to expand AI use.

stories.title: Brazilian court blocks Meta from using news publishers' content for AI training as a condition of platform use

articles.title: Brasilien: Gericht verbietet Meta die Nutzung von Medieninhalten für KI-Training

facts.fact: A court in Sao Paulo barred Meta from using content from media companies belonging to three Brazilian press associations for AI training (heise, citing AFP reports).
Judge Guilherme Madeira Dezem issued the preliminary injunction after suits by ANJ (newspapers), Abert (radio and TV) and Aner (magazines).
Meta's new business terms, due to take effect on November 20, made handing over content free of charge a condition of continued platform use.
The court called forcing media to hand over copyrighted material for free, like a 'toll' to stay present on channels, an 'obvious abuse of rights', and suspended that part of the terms.
Meta may not penalise outlets that reject the terms; a violation costs 1 million reais (EUR 162,000) a day.
ANJ called it a first success in defending intellectual property and the sustainability of professional journalism.
heise notes the New York Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft over AI training since late 2023.

stories.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve, open-source proof that an AI answer came from the model you were promised

articles.title: 앤트로픽, AI 모델 '신원 확인' 기술 공개...클로드가 개발 과정 주도

facts.fact: Anthropic released FlashProve on Nov 2 (US time), an open-source system using zero-knowledge proofs (zkSNARK) to verify a response came from a specified model without revealing its weights.
It aims to catch a provider swapping in a cheaper model or tampering with outputs; it verifies the computation, not whether the answer is true.
Claude helped develop it by applying existing cryptography tools to improve efficiency; Anthropic published the Claude-written protocol spec and says researchers did not review it in detail.
Test on the 400-billion-parameter Llama 4 Maverick (4-bit weights) used one H100 GPU; proof size about 19 MB and verification about 17 seconds on 24 CPU threads.
Proof generation needed 70-95x the GPU time of ordinary prefill in vLLM under specific conditions; current implementation uses a 1,024-token context, so it is not production-ready.

stories.title: Meta acquires Conductor, a coding-agent coordination startup
stories.repeat: no (already a candidate in ops/candidates/2026-11-05.json, not posted)

facts.fact: Meta acquired Conductor, a San Francisco startup (founded 2024) whose software coordinates multiple AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex in separate workspaces; Axios reported first and Meta confirmed.
Conductor advertised more than 100,000 users and builds no models of its own.
Conductor's cloud service ends November 20; the local Mac app is phased out from early 2027.
Meta launched Muse Code in August, the Muse agent in September and Muse Wonder models in October, and is seeking revenue beyond ads to offset AI spending.
